_protocol.purpose: Single source of truth for every agent and app working on this project (Claude, Melius agent Mel, ElevenLabs, Metricool, humans). Read it before any task; append what you changed at the end.
_protocol.public_notice: The repository is public. Never put passwords, API keys, signed media URLs, emails, payment or personal data in this file.
at_task_start: Load the newest version of this file (raw URL). Read _protocol, open_tasks, the last 10 changelog entries, and the sections for your app.
Copy identity.anchor_paragraph, quality_lock and voice settings VERBATIM. Never paraphrase or re-describe them; drift comes from paraphrasing.
If the task spends credits or money, quote the cost from apps.<app>.costs before running and stop if it exceeds budget.per_step_cap or the user's quote.
at_task_end: Append ONE entry to changelog (never edit or delete old entries) and bump version (patch +1).
Update the affected objects (clips[].status, node ids, open_tasks) in place.

If you cannot write files (Mel inside Melius, ElevenLabs), print the entry as a fenced JSON block headed 'HANDOFF ENTRY' so the user can paste it to an agent that can write (Claude: `python project/project_state.py log --from-json entry.json`).

changed: what changed, one item per line
next: what the next agent should do

recipe.voice_name: Veda Sky - Friendly, Warm and Clear
recipe.settings: platform defaults; do not change stability/similarity/style; no speed change
recipe.text: the plain script line only: no audio tags, no <break>, no voice description, no stage directions

rejected: letting a video model invent the voice without an audio reference
take_selection: v3 varies take to take: generate, then check duration fits the planned clip (vo + 0.4 s <= clip length)
same-speaker check: stitch [market clip + new clip] and ask a listener model for a 1-10 similarity score; keep only 9-10, re-roll otherwise (a re-roll costs ~120 credits)
voice.delivery: warm, clear, relaxed, friendly; talking to one friend; no announcer energy

timing.why: Every lip-sync failure so far came from footage and voice being made for different recordings. The mouth must be generated FROM the final voice file.
rules: 1. Write the line: 2.3-2.6 spoken words per second of speech (6 s clip ~ 13-15 words).
2. Generate the final VO FIRST (voice.recipe). Measure its duration D (ms) from the audio node.
3. Clip length = ceil(D/1000 + 0.4) whole seconds (Seedance takes integers 3-15). Resulting silent tail 0.4-1.0 s; if the tail would exceed 1.2 s, trim or re-roll the take.
4. Render the video WITH that exact VO wired as the audio input (native lip sync). Never render first and re-sync a different or re-rolled VO later.
5. Shot breakdown in the prompt uses the VO's own phrase times (run `python project/project_state.py beats --clip N` or estimate by characters) and ends with 'closed-mouth hold' for the tail.
6. If VO > clip length the last word is cut; if VO < original speech in re-used footage the mouth keeps moving without sound. Both are rejects.
7. Post-lip-sync (Kling etc.) is only a rescue for a few frames, and only when the new VO starts and ends within ±0.2 s of the speech in the footage.
qc: voice starts within 0.4 s of first lip movement
lips never move while no voice is heard
no voice while lips are closed

gravity_and_weight: Everything has weight: held bags pull the forearm down and swing a little then settle; a lifted object rises slower than it falls.
Walking: heel then toe, weight transfers with each step, head and shoulders dip 1-2 cm per step, the handheld frame bobs in rhythm; feet never slide, no gliding.
Hair: long platinum hair hangs straight when still, swings with a head turn and settles after about half a second; strands follow the stated wind direction only.
Fabric: heavy wool swings slowly and creases at elbows; nylon shells rustle and crease; knit collars sit, they do not float.
Boardwalk planks dip a few millimetres under each step; wet cobbles and paving show reflections that move with the camera.
Breathing: small chest rise; after exertion faster for the first seconds, then settles.
Cold: breath vapour only at about 5 °C or below; steam off hair/skin after sauna rises and drifts downwind and fades within a second.
Water and rain: drizzle falls straight or with the stated wind; droplets bead on waxed fabric; puddles ripple on impact.
Camera: genuine handheld phone, small shake, one autofocus breath allowed; never a gimbal, never a crane.
physics.one_rule_per_clip: Name the single physics rule the clip lives or dies by in TOP PRIORITY.

method: Decide place, date and time; find where the sun or main light is; decide which way she faces; therefore which cheek is lit.
Write KEY (source, side of frame, colour temperature), FILL (sky/ambient), BOUNCE (colour from the biggest nearby surface onto a named body part).
Shadows: contact shadows under what she touches, all shadows fall the same direction as the scene's own shadows.
She is never brighter than the environment; light is constant for the whole take (not a time-lapse).
Always 'discard reference lighting': the face anchor is a studio image and its light must not leak in.
lighting.template: RELIGHT: discard reference lighting. Key: [SOURCE] from [SIDE], [WARM/COOL]. Fill: [SKY/AMBIENT]. Bounce: [COLOUR] from [SURFACE] onto her [CHEEK/JAW/CHIN]. Shadows fall [DIRECTION] like the scene's shadows. Never brighter than the environment; light constant.

quality_lock.text:
QUALITY LOCK (applies to the whole take and overrides anything above that conflicts with it):
- Framing: tight vertical framing from mid-chest up for the whole take. Her fingers, the phone and her feet are never in frame. Only her head, neck, shoulders and upper chest (plus any prop named above), with the real place behind her.
- Skin: unretouched phone footage. Her light-brown freckles are clearly visible across the nose bridge and upper cheeks in every frame, with real skin texture, fine pores and slight natural unevenness; no smoothing, no beauty filter, no waxy look.
- Ears: her platinum hair is tucked behind one ear so ONE small plain gold hoop earring is clearly visible on that ear; exactly one hoop per ear, never doubled, never a stud, cuff or second ring.
- Brows: ash-brown, clearly darker than her platinum hair, in every frame. Hair stays cool platinum, never golden.
- Mouth and timing: the provided audio is her whole performance. Her lips move precisely with every word of it, from the first word to the last, and ONLY while a word is being spoken. In any silence (before the first word, in pauses, and after the last word) her lips are closed and still. After the last word her mouth closes softly and stays closed until the end of the clip; she may only smile gently with closed lips. Her voice is exactly the voice in the provided audio, same timbre, pitch and pace; never re-voiced, never faster or slower.
- Movement: only when the action says she walks, her head and shoulders dip gently with each step and the frame shakes slightly with each footfall, never gliding. When she stands or the phone is propped, only small breathing movement and natural head motion.
- Clothing and background: all clothing is completely plain, with no text, letters, logos, badges or labels anywhere. Background people stay small, far away and soft-focus, with stable bodies that never merge into walls or objects; buildings and walls are rigid and never shift or bend.
- Camera: genuine phone footage, small natural shake; not a gimbal.
- Identity: her face stays identical to the identity reference from the first to the last frame; no morphing.
quality_lock.rule: wire as a text input into every video node (Melius appends it to the prompt)

mechanics_learned: Stitch needs at least 2 connected sources; output length = longest of visuals and overlays (a longer overlay adds a black tail). Stitch upscales to 1080x1920.
An audio node cannot take a video node's sound (no audio extraction from video).
Gemini 3.1 Pro and Qwen text nodes accept only ONE video input; to compare two clips, stitch them first.
Kling lip-sync keeps the source length; audio longer than the video is cut; where the audio is silent the ORIGINAL mouth motion stays.
sonilo-video-sfx-mix replaced the voice in a test; use sonilo-video-sfx (separate audio) + stitch overlay instead.
Seedance 2.0 re-renders the voice from the audio reference; the market clip's published voice came out of this process.
Duration on a stitch node is ignored (cannot trim).
AI QC (Gemini) hallucinates timing and defects; the user's eyes decide timing; use two different models and count a blocker only when both agree.
